stem: A 5-year-old girl is brought to the office by her mother because she "sunburns too easily."  The patient's skin becomes red and scaly with only minimal sun exposure.  The mother has avoided exposing her child to excess sunlight since infancy but finds it difficult now that the patient has begun kindergarten.  Physical examination shows dry, thin skin with numerous irregularly pigmented macules on the face and dorsum of the hands.  This patient's disorder is most likely caused by a primary defect in which of the following processes?​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌
explanation:
This patient's severe sun sensitivity and mottled pigmentation are characteristic of xeroderma pigmentosum (XP), a rare autosomal recessive disorder in which defective nucleotide excision repair leads to the accumulation of DNA damage induced by ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

UV radiation induces the formation of pyrimidine (usually thymine) dimers, covalent intrastrand cross-links between adjacent bases that distort the double helix and block DNA replication beyond the site of dimerization.  Nucleotide excision repair normally removes these lesions: helicases unwind the DNA surrounding the distorted segment, endonucleases incise the damaged strand on either side of the lesion, and DNA polymerase and ligase fill and seal the resulting gap.  In XP, mutations in the genes encoding these enzymes impair nucleotide excision repair.  Pyrimidine dimers and other bulky carcinogenic adducts consequently accumulate, generating the mutations that drive malignant transformation.

The skin is normal at birth, but severe sun sensitivity (eg, erythema, scaling) of exposed areas, especially the face, develops within the first year of life.  Chronic UV damage subsequently produces poikiloderma (atrophy, telangiectasias, and intermingled areas of hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation).  Many patients also have ocular involvement (eg, photophobia, conjunctival injection, keratitis).  Cutaneous malignancies (eg, squamous and basal cell carcinoma, melanoma) can develop as early as age 5.

(Choice A)  Defective repair of DNA interstrand cross-links, which join nucleotides on opposing DNA strands, occurs in Fanconi anemia (eg, short stature, absent or hypoplastic thumbs, bone marrow failure, increased malignancy risk).  In contrast, UV radiation generates intrastrand cross-links between adjacent nucleotides on the same strand.

(Choice B)  Defective DNA mismatch repair causes accumulation of mismatched bases generated by erroneous DNA replication rather than by UV exposure.  It is associated with hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (Lynch syndrome), which predisposes to colorectal, endometrial, and ovarian malignancy.

(Choices D and E)  p53 halts cell cycle progression when DNA is damaged, allowing time for repair; irreversible damage triggers apoptosis.  Acquired p53 mutations are found in many spontaneous cancers, whereas inherited p53 mutations cause Li-Fraumeni syndrome (wide range of malignancies at a young age).  However, Li-Fraumeni syndrome does not cause photosensitivity and the primary defect in XP is impaired nucleotide excision repair, not cell cycle or apoptosis regulation.

Educational objective:Xeroderma pigmentosum is caused by defective nucleotide excision repair, which prevents removal of ultraviolet radiation–induced DNA damage (eg, pyrimidine dimers).  Affected patients develop severe sun sensitivity, mottled hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation with skin atrophy, and cutaneous malignancies beginning in childhood.​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​​​​​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌
